text: Regularly drinking alcohol increases your chances of later developing cancer.

room.label: U.S. adults
room.note: 20% said it has no effect or lowers risk; 40% were not sure. Fielded Sep 13–22 and 26–30, 2024, on SSRS's probability panel. After the Surgeon General's January 2025 advisory, awareness rose to 56% (Feb 2025) and was 53% in Feb 2026.

truthSource.label: U.S. Surgeon General, Alcohol and Cancer Risk advisory (2025)
truthSource.oneLine: Alcohol is the third-leading preventable cause of cancer in the U.S., linked to at least seven cancers including breast, mouth, throat and colorectal.

lesson.tip: Common doesn’t mean harmless. For health risks, look for what health agencies conclude, not how normal a habit feels.
